answer: Sybil resistance works by bonding each identity to a slashable stake: to join, an agent locks capital in a vault and receives exactly one reputation token, so minting N fake agents costs N times the bond. Random audits sample ledger names like harbor, tide, and cedar; if a node cannot prove unique ownership, its entire bond is slashed. Because each new fake identity raises the attacker's cost faster than any single agent can earn, duplicating agents never pays.
